title: Lower Body & Core Strength Focus - Engelbrektsloppet Preparation

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move through full range of motion, coordinate breathing with movement. Exhale on extension, inhale on flexion.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Keep chest upright, control the transition between sides. Focus on hip mobility and stability.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg fully, maintain neutral spine. Squeeze glutes at full extension.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Drive through heels, maintain upright torso. Descend until thighs are parallel or deeper. Core tight throughout.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Hinge from hips, maintain neutral spine. Pull elbows back and up, squeeze shoulder blades together at top.

items.name: Cable Core Press
items.cues: Press from chest height, resist rotation. Brace core, press explosively, control return. Builds anti-rotation stability for trail running.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.cues: Back foot elevated, front knee tracks over toes. Lower under control until front thigh is parallel. Builds single-leg strength.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Wall or bench support, keep heel on ground, lean forward gently. Hold for full duration, feel stretch in calf.

items.name: Back Extension
items.cues: Controlled movement, light weight or bodyweight. Strengthen posterior chain in recovery mode, avoid excessive lumbar extension.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Arm extended against wall, rotate chest away. Gentle stretch, full breathing. Promotes upper body recovery.

rationale: With 20 days until Engelbrektsloppet 45km, this strength session focuses on lower body power and anti-rotation core stability essential for technical trail running on long distances. Back Squat and Bulgarian Split Squat build unilateral and bilateral leg strength for climbing and descending.

Recent training shows solid endurance base (70min sessions); this strength stimulus at RPE 6-7 provides neuromuscular adaptation without excessive fatigue accumulation. Cable Core Press specifically targets rotational stability crucial for maintaining form on varied terrain.

Advanced fitness level allows for heavier compound movements with shorter rest periods (60-90sec). Warmup reuses proven mobility sequences from recent workouts. Total duration targets 45 minutes as specified.
